# # Map customer axum auth middleware bypassed for tracing-instrumented routes to the Router / tower ServiceBuilder layer-order boundary

A customer reports that their axum service has an auth middleware
that runs on most routes but is silently bypassed for routes nested
under a Router that wraps a tracing layer. Requests to those routes
succeed without the Authorization header; the auth layer never
produces a span.

Your task:
1. Find where axum's Router applies layers and how nested Routers
   compose with tower::ServiceBuilder layers.
2. Find where tower::ServiceBuilder enforces layer order and how
   .layer() differs from .route_layer() in axum.
3. Trace the cross-repo path: axum::Router::route_layer vs
   axum::Router::layer -> Router::merge -> tower::ServiceBuilder ->
   tower::Layer::layer composition. Cite each file and the function
   responsible.
4. Identify why route_layer() applied to a parent Router does NOT
   wrap routes added via Router::merge from a sub-router, leaving
   the auth layer skipped for nested routes.


Search only these repositories: github.com/sg-evals/axum--axum-v0.7.5, github.com/sg-evals/tower--tower-0.4.13

Here is the complete trace of the bug.

---

## 1. How `Router::layer` vs `Router::route_layer` work

Both are defined in [axum/src/routing/mod.rs](./r/github.com/sg-evals/axum--axum-v0.7.5/-/blob/axum/src/routing/mod.rs?L274-L307).

**`Router::layer`** ([L274-L289](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/axum--axum-v0.7.5/-/blob/axum/src/routing/mod.rs?L274-L289)) wraps *everything*: the `path_router`, the `fallback_router`, and the `catch_all_fallback`:

```rust
pub fn layer<L>(self, layer: L) -> Router<S> {
    self.map_inner(|this| RouterInner {
        path_router: this.path_router.layer(layer.clone()),
        fallback_router: this.fallback_router.layer(layer.clone()),
        default_fallback: this.default_fallback,
        catch_all_fallback: this.catch_all_fallback.map(|route| route.layer(layer)),
    })
}
```

**`Router::route_layer`** ([L291-L307](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/axum--axum-v0.7.5/-/blob/axum/src/routing/mod.rs?L291-L307)) wraps *only* the `path_router`. The `fallback_router` and `catch_all_fallback` are passed through untouched:

```rust
pub fn route_layer<L>(self, layer: L) -> Self {
    self.map_inner(|this| RouterInner {
        path_router: this.path_router.route_layer(layer),
        fallback_router: this.fallback_router,          // unchanged
        default_fallback: this.default_fallback,
        catch_all_fallback: this.catch_all_fallback,    // unchanged
    })
}
```

The intent is that `route_layer` prevents a 404 from being converted to a 401 by skipping the fallback. But both share the same critical constraint: **the layer is applied only to routes that are already registered at the moment of the call.**

---

## 2. `PathRouter::route_layer` — the snapshot-at-call-time mechanic

[`PathRouter::route_layer`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/axum--axum-v0.7.5/-/blob/axum/src/routing/path_router.rs?L264-L294) iterates `self.routes` — a `HashMap<RouteId, Endpoint>` — and calls `endpoint.layer(layer.clone())` for each entry currently present:

```rust
pub(super) fn route_layer<L>(self, layer: L) -> Self {
    if self.routes.is_empty() {
        panic!("Adding a route_layer before any routes is a no-op. ...");
    }

    let routes = self
        .routes
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(id, endpoint)| {
            let route = endpoint.layer(layer.clone());   // wraps each existing Route
            (id, route)
        })
        .collect();

    PathRouter { routes, node: self.node, prev_route_id: self.prev_route_id }
}
```

The returned `PathRouter` contains a new `routes` map where each `Route` has the layer baked in. **This is a one-time transformation, not a registry that wraps future insertions.** Equally, `PathRouter::layer` at [L240-L262](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/axum--axum-v0.7.5/-/blob/axum/src/routing/path_router.rs?L240-L262) works the same way.

---

## 3. `Route::layer` — how layers are actually composed per-route

Each `Route` is a `BoxCloneService` stored in a `Mutex` ([route.rs L31](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/axum--axum-v0.7.5/-/blob/axum/src/routing/route.rs?L31)). `Route::layer` ([L52-L69](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/axum--axum-v0.7.5/-/blob/axum/src/routing/route.rs?L52-L69)) constructs a new `Route` by composing the given layer with the existing service:

```rust
pub(crate) fn layer<L, NewError>(self, layer: L) -> Route<NewError> {
    let layer = (
        MapRequestLayer::new(...),
        MapErrLayer::new(Into::into),
        MapResponseLayer::new(IntoResponse::into_response),
        layer,         // <-- the actual auth/tracing layer
    );
    Route::new(layer.layer(self))   // produces a new BoxCloneService
}
```

This delegates to tower's `Stack` composition.

---

## 4. tower `ServiceBuilder::layer` and `Stack` composition

[`ServiceBuilder::layer`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tower--tower-0.4.13/-/blob/tower/src/builder/mod.rs?L132-L136) prepends each new layer onto a `Stack`:

```rust
pub fn layer<T>(self, layer: T) -> ServiceBuilder<Stack<T, L>> {
    ServiceBuilder { layer: Stack::new(layer, self.layer) }
}
```

[`Stack::layer`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tower--tower-0.4.13/-/blob/tower-layer/src/stack.rs?L25-L29) applies inner first, then outer:

```rust
fn layer(&self, service: S) -> Self::Service {
    let inner = self.inner.layer(service);  // inner layer wraps service
    self.outer.layer(inner)                 // outer layer wraps that
}
```

This means layers added *first* to a `ServiceBuilder` end up *outermost* in the call stack. Axum uses this same `Layer::layer` protocol in `Route::layer`, so the `auth_layer` passed to `route_layer` is permanently composed into the `BoxCloneService` at the time of the call.

---

## 5. `Router::merge` — why it bypasses the already-applied layer

[`Router::merge`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/axum--axum-v0.7.5/-/blob/axum/src/routing/mod.rs?L224-L272) calls `this.path_router.merge(path_router)`. [`PathRouter::merge`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/axum--axum-v0.7.5/-/blob/axum/src/routing/path_router.rs?L123-L161) iterates the *other* router's endpoints and calls `self.route(path, method_router)` or `self.route_service(path, route)` for each:

```rust
for (id, route) in routes {
    // ...
    match route {
        Endpoint::MethodRouter(method_router) => self.route(path, method_router)?,
        Endpoint::Route(route) => self.route_service(path, route)?,
    }
}
```

These are bare insertions into `self.routes`. **No layer is applied during merge.** The merged routes land in the `HashMap` as raw `Endpoint` values, identical to how they were stored in the sub-router — with no knowledge of any layer that was previously applied to the parent router's `PathRouter`.

---

## Root cause summary

The bug arises from this ordering dependency:

```
parent = Router::new()
    .route("/parent-route", get(handler))
    .route_layer(auth_layer)     // snapshot: wraps only /parent-route's Route
    .merge(sub_router);          // sub_router's routes inserted AFTER snapshot
                                 // -> no auth_layer baked into them
```

`route_layer` (and `layer`) apply by **iterating and transforming the current `routes` HashMap** at call time — they do not install a registry or interceptor that wraps future insertions. When `merge` later inserts the sub-router's routes, it calls `self.route(...)` directly with the sub-router's unwrapped `Endpoint`s. There is no mechanism to retroactively apply the parent's layer.

The fix is to call `.route_layer(auth_layer)` **after** `.merge(sub_router)`:

```rust
let app = Router::new()
    .route("/parent-route", get(handler))
    .merge(sub_router)           // all routes present first
    .route_layer(auth_layer);    // now wraps ALL of them
```

Or apply the auth layer on the sub-router itself before merging, so its routes already carry the layer when they are inserted into the parent's `PathRouter`.
